recent_posts.title: A Real Multi-Agent Platform by JPMorgan
recent_posts.summary: JPMorgan's investment research team details the architecture of 'Ask David', their production multi-agent AI system built with LangGraph. The system uses a supervisor agent to orchestrate specialized subagents handling retrieval, structured data, and analytics. It incorporates an LLM-as-judge reflection node for quality control and human-in-the-loop for final accuracy checks. The platform integrates structured databases, unstructured documents, and proprietary analytics to deliver real-time insights for financial advisors analyzing thousands of financial products.

recent_posts.title: Context Is The New King In AI!
recent_posts.summary: A high-level overview tracing the evolution of AI retrieval systems from basic RAG to Advanced RAG to Agentic RAG, culminating in the concept of Context Engineering. The post argues that context orchestration — combining memory, retrieval, tools, and state — is the next frontier for building effective AI agents, positioning 'context' as the most critical element in modern AI systems.

recent_posts.title: Automate Your Developer Workflows with MCP!
recent_posts.summary: Port's MCP Connector acts as a single governed entry point for AI hosts like Claude, ChatGPT, and Cursor to access multiple developer tools (GitHub, Grafana, Snowflake, Slack, etc.) via the Model Context Protocol. Instead of maintaining separate MCP server connections, platform engineers route all external MCP servers through Port, controlling which tools and servers are exposed per team while respecting existing OAuth permissions. Developers and AI agents get one unified interface grounded in an engineering knowledge graph with just-in-time data from external systems.

recent_posts.title: Agentic AI Architecture for Developers
recent_posts.summary: An overview of agentic AI architecture for developers, explaining the difference between generative AI and agentic AI, the five core capabilities of agentic systems (perception, reasoning, action, learning, collaboration), and how agents process instructions using prompts, knowledge, and skills. Includes links to hands-on guides for building agentic apps with LangGraph and MCP.

recent_posts.title: Prompt Engineering vs Context Engineering
recent_posts.summary: Context engineering is positioned as more important than prompt engineering for building reliable AI agents. Rather than crafting better prompts, the argument is that teams should invest in 'context lakes' — structured, accessible, live data about service ownership, deployment history, staging health, and approval gates. When an AI system has rich context before it starts, vague instructions become precise executable actions without hallucinations. The core claim: the bottleneck in agentic systems is the environment the model operates in, not the model itself.

recent_posts.title: Scaling Agentic AI in Enterprises
recent_posts.summary: An overview of the key architectural components needed to deploy agentic AI systems in enterprise environments. Covers AI gateways as central orchestrators, LLM fine-tuning and deployment, MCP servers for tool integration, Agent-to-Agent (A2A) communication protocols, guardrails for safety and compliance, and integrations with providers like OpenAI, Anthropic, AWS Bedrock, and Azure. The post links to a full blog article and a hands-on video guide.

recent_posts.title: Context Engineering is the Future of AI Agents!
recent_posts.summary: Context engineering is presented as the evolution beyond prompt engineering and RAG for AI agents. While prompt engineering focuses on crafting inputs and RAG augments LLMs with database-retrieved data, context engineering goes further by supplying agents with data, instructions, tools, APIs, memory, and more. The post argues that AI agents need this richer context to reason and act effectively in production, and promotes Port.io as a 'context lake' solution for agentic systems.

recent_posts.title: Build reliable AI workflows with agentic primitives and context engineering
recent_posts.summary: Context engineering is presented as a key discipline for building reliable AI workflows. Five techniques are outlined: session splitting (separating planning, implementation, and testing into distinct agent sessions), modular instructions (targeted .instructions.md files), cognitive focus optimization (.chatmode.md files), memory-driven development (.memory.md files), and context helpers (.context.md & skills.md files). The post also promotes Port.io as a context management platform.

recent_posts.title: You need a contextual semantic layer for your Agentic AI systems.
recent_posts.summary: Traditional semantic layers designed for dashboards and static reporting fall short for agentic AI systems. A contextual semantic layer acts as an intelligent middle layer between raw data sources (cloud warehouses, transactional DBs, operational systems, unstructured data) and downstream consumers. It passes data through four governing layers — Metrics & Data Model, Ontology Layer, Context + Memory, and Knowledge Graph — adding structure, business meaning, and reasoning capability. This enriched data then powers AI agents, BI dashboards, AI analytics tools, and embedded data apps.

recent_posts.title: What is Agent Harness?
recent_posts.summary: Agent Harness is argued to be a rebranding of classic system design principles applied to AI agents. Concepts like routing logic, tool calling, memory/context, agent loops, and observability map directly to familiar patterns: service routers, API gateways, caches, event-driven architectures, and standard logging. The core claim is that engineers who already understand system design already understand agent harnesses — they just need to apply those patterns to LLM-powered components.
